---
title: "Feature selection"
---

## Scope and status {#sec-fs-scope}

This chapter builds the gene panel on which the covariances of
@sec-cov-scope are estimated. It runs on the single-cell counts of
GSE229513 at the three bulk-matched times (@sec-geo-design), one time
at a time. What the panel must achieve, and why each step is there, is
stated in the feature-selection vignette
([3.1, estimand](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-estimand)):
genes whose type-level moments can be estimated in every type and that
carry information about $\boldsymbol{p}$. The ranking statistics below
are computed inside one specimen. They calibrate a screen, not a
population-level claim of differential expression (@nte-pseudoreplication).

Ranks are computed on `SCTransform` Pearson residuals or on a count
GLM. Neither scale is exported: the moments that enter DeCovarT are on
the linear scale
([2.1, normalisation](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/02-1-single-cell-generative-optimisation.html#sec-norm-linear)).

| Step | Section | Code | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cell and gene QC | @sec-fs-qc | `scripts/01_01_prepare_and_filter_genes_sctransform.R`, section 1 | run; outputs dated 2026-09-28 to 2026-10-01 |
| `SCTransform` v2 fit per time | @sec-fs-sct | `R/rank_sctransform_naive.R::rank_genes_sctransform()` | run |
| Between/within ratio rank (current) | @sec-fs-ms-ratio | same | run |
| Presence gate | @sec-fs-presence | `R/rank_genes_omnibus.R::presence_gate()` | written, not run |
| Omnibus count-model rank (new) | @sec-fs-omnibus | `R/rank_genes_omnibus.R::rank_genes_omnibus()` | written, not run |
| 48 h bulk consistency filter | @sec-fs-bulk-consistency | `R/bulk_consistency.R::bulk_consistency_filter()` | written, not run |
| Export of the top 500 per time | @sec-fs-export | `scripts/01_03_export_equal_type_seurat.R` | run on the current rank |
| Optional NSGA-II refinement | @sec-fs-nsga2 | `scripts/04_02_feature_selection_genetic_algorithm.R` | template only |

: Feature-selection steps, code and status. "Written, not run" means the function exists and parses but no output has been produced in this repository. {#tbl-fs-status}

The current panel (top 500 per time, @sec-fs-export) comes from the
between/within ratio. Once the presence gate, the omnibus rank and the
bulk filter have been run, they replace that rank as steps 3 to 5 of
@fig-pipeline, and every output of @sec-cov-scope has to be refitted.

## Cell and gene QC as applied {#sec-fs-qc}

The tiers of quality control recommended in the vignette
([3.1, QC](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-qc))
are applied only in part. What runs today is listed here.

**Cells.**

- The authors' Seurat QC (`scater`, @sec-seurat) is taken as given.
- `01_01` keeps cells with a time slot in {48 h, 72 h, 96 h}, a
  non-missing `celltypeannotation`, and a library size above zero.
- The culture-stress labels flagged `include_in_ranking = FALSE` in
  `data/dictionaries/suppinger_celltype_crosswalk.csv` (Cd63+
  ectoderm-like artefact, Zscan4+ artefact) are dropped before the
  fit.
- A type with fewer than `min_cells = 20` cells in a slot stays in the
  `SCTransform` fit and is left out of the scores. Exiting naïve
  pluripotency at 72 h (8 cells) is the only such case.
- No library-size MAD filter, detected-gene filter or mitochondrial
  filter is applied by this repository. This is the gap with tier (i)
  of the vignette.

**Genes.**

- The allow-list is the gene set of the authors' `SCT` counts layer:
  2,944 of the 27,027 genes of the RNA assay. Genes outside it never
  enter a fit.
- After the per-time fit, `SCTransform` returns residuals for 2,892
  (48 h), 2,769 (72 h) and 2,811 (96 h) genes (`model_card.csv`).
- Ribosomal, mitochondrial and sex-chromosome genes are not removed
  explicitly; whether the authors' allow-list already excludes them has
  not been checked.

| Time | Cell type | Cells | Scored |
|---|---|---:|---|
| 48 h | Epiblast | 10,590 | yes |
| 48 h | Exiting naïve pluripotency | 265 | yes |
| 48 h | Naïve pluripotency | 36 | yes |
| 48 h | Zscan4+ artefact | 44 | no (artefact) |
| 72 h | Primitive streak | 4,279 | yes |
| 72 h | Ectopic pluripotency | 266 | yes |
| 72 h | Naïve pluripotency | 66 | yes |
| 72 h | Cd63+ ectoderm-like artefact | 100 | no (artefact) |
| 72 h | Exiting naïve pluripotency | 8 | no (fewer than 20 cells) |
| 96 h | Pre-somitic mesoderm | 3,589 | yes |
| 96 h | Caudal mesoderm | 1,061 | yes |
| 96 h | Gut | 140 | yes |
| 96 h | Ectopic pluripotency | 116 | yes |
| 96 h | Somite differentiation front | 29 | yes |

: Cells per type and time after the slot filter (`output/naive_marker_selection/tables/cell_counts.csv`). The eleven scored type × time cells are the units of @sec-cov-scope. {#tbl-fs-cell-counts}

## Presence gate {#sec-fs-presence}

A gene enters the ranking at a given time only if it is detected, and
varies, in **every** scored type at that time. With $\delta_{gj}$ the
fraction of cells of type $j$ with a non-zero count for gene $g$, and
$v_{gj}$ the within-type variance of the counts,

$$
\min_{j}\delta_{gj}\ge\delta_{\min}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\min_{j}v_{gj}>0 .
$$ {#eq-fs-presence}

`presence_gate()` in `R/rank_genes_omnibus.R` returns the logical
gene vector; $\delta_{\min}$ is an argument fixed before the ranks are
seen (the sketch below uses 0.05). The reasons for a gate in every
type, rather than in at least one, are in
[3.1, presence](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-presence).
In the current outputs the gate is absent. Its absence is one cause of
the constant-gene fallback described in @sec-cov-stale.

## `SCTransform` v2 fit per time {#sec-fs-sct}

`rank_genes_sctransform()` refits `Seurat::SCTransform()` separately at
48 h, 72 h and 96 h (`split_by = "time_point"`) on the allow-list
genes. Cells of every non-artefact type at that time are fitted
together. The fitted mean is an intercept plus a library-size offset,

$$
\log\mu_{gc}
=
\beta_{0g}
+
\log s_{c},
\qquad
x_{gc}\sim\mathrm{NB}(\mu_{gc},\psi_{g}),
$$ {#eq-fs-v2-offset}

with $s_{c}$ the full RNA library size of cell $c$ (column sum of the
unfiltered count matrix, stored as `log_umi` $=\log_{10}s_{c}$), not the
sum over the allow-list. The Pearson residual is
$r_{gc}=(x_{gc}-\hat\mu_{gc})/\sqrt{\hat\mu_{gc}+\hat\mu_{gc}^{2}/\hat\psi_{g}}$.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| `vst.flavor` | `"v2"` (depth slope fixed at $\ln 10$ on $\log_{10}s_c$, i.e. an offset) |
| `method` | `"glmGamPoi"`; fitter recorded as `glmGamPoi_offset` |
| `vars.to.regress` | none |
| Cell type, cell line in the fit | no, no |
| `ncells` | all retained cells of the slot (10,891 at 48 h, 4,619 at 72 h, 4,935 at 96 h) |
| `residual.features` | all allow-list genes; `return.only.var.genes = FALSE` |
| `do.correct.umi`, `do.scale`, `do.center` | `FALSE`, `FALSE`, `TRUE` |
| `seed.use` | 1 |
| Residual clip | $\pm\sqrt{n/30}$: $\pm 19.05$ (48 h), $\pm 12.41$ (72 h), $\pm 12.83$ (96 h) |

: `SCTransform` settings as run (`model_card.csv`, `R/rank_sctransform_naive.R`). {#tbl-fs-sct-settings}

Cell type is left out of the fit on purpose; the vignette discusses
the alternative of fitting `~ cell_type`
([3.1, consistency](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-consistency)).
The omnibus rank of @sec-fs-omnibus tests the cell-type effect
directly on the counts instead.

## Current rank: between/within ratio {#sec-fs-ms-ratio}

The residual matrix of one slot is split by type. With $C_j$ cells of
type $j$, $\bar r_{gj}$ the mean residual of gene $g$ in type $j$, and
$v_{gj}$ its within-type variance, the two decompositions are

$$
\mathrm{SS}_{\mathrm{between},g}
=
\sum_{j=1}^{J}C_{j}\bigl(\bar r_{gj}-\bar r_{g}\bigr)^{2},
\qquad
\mathrm{SS}_{\mathrm{within},g}
=
\sum_{j=1}^{J}\sum_{c\in j}\bigl(r_{gc}-\bar r_{gj}\bigr)^{2}
$$ {#eq-fs-ss}

(every cell has weight one), and

$$
\bar r_{g}^{\mathrm{eq}}
=
J^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{J}\bar r_{gj},
\qquad
\mathrm{MS}_{\mathrm{between},g}
=
J^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{J}(\bar r_{gj}-\bar r_{g}^{\mathrm{eq}})^{2},
\qquad
\mathrm{MS}_{\mathrm{within},g}
=
J^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{J}v_{gj}
$$ {#eq-fs-equal-type}

(every type has weight $1/J$). The score is the ratio of the between
term to the within term. What this ratio estimates, and how it relates
to a score test of the type effect, is in
[3.1, consistency](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-consistency).

Three lists are built per slot (`anova_ss()`, `anova_ms_equal_type()`,
`rank_ratio()`):

1. **Global, equal cell weight.** Top `n_genes_global = 500` genes by
   $\mathrm{SS}_{\mathrm{between}}/\mathrm{SS}_{\mathrm{within}}$
   (`ranks_global.csv`). The largest type dominates.
2. **Global, equal type weight.** Top 500 by
   $\mathrm{MS}_{\mathrm{between}}/\mathrm{MS}_{\mathrm{within}}$
   (`ranks_global_equal_type.csv`). This list feeds the export of
   @sec-fs-export.
3. **Per cell type.** One-versus-rest split, top
   `n_genes_celltype = 50` genes by the equal-cell ratio
   (`ranks_per_cell_type.csv`). The flag
   $\mathrm{SS}_{\mathrm{between}}>\mathrm{SS}_{\mathrm{within}}$ is
   stored and not used as a gate: on unit-variance residuals it is an
   $R^{2}>1/2$ cut, which almost no gene meets when one type dominates
   the slot.

Each list is then united with the signalling markers of the types
scored in that slot (@sec-fs-markers).

| Time | Shared by lists 1 and 2 (of 500) |
|---|---:|
| 48 h | 313 |
| 72 h | 326 |
| 96 h | 372 |

: Overlap of the equal-cell and equal-type top 500 (`global_weighting_overlap.csv`). {#tbl-fs-weighting-overlap}

At 48 h the leading equal-cell ratios land on naïve-pluripotency
markers; at 96 h the top gene is the endoderm marker *Sox17*. The
residual clip changes only the far tail of these ratios.

## Omnibus count-model rank {#sec-fs-omnibus}

`rank_genes_omnibus()` (`R/rank_genes_omnibus.R`) replaces the residual
ratio by a test of the cell-type main effect on the counts, then ranks
the genes that pass by effect size. Per time slot, on the genes that
pass the presence gate:

1. Fit the negative-binomial GLM $\log\mu_{gc}=\beta_{0g}+\beta_{g,j(c)}+\log s_{c}$
   with `glmGamPoi::glm_gp(design = ~ cell_type, offset = log(s_c))`
   [@glmGamPoi2020]. The offset is the full library size;
   `size_factors` is switched off so that it is not applied twice.
2. Test the joint type effect with `glmGamPoi::test_de(fit, reduced_design = ~ 1)`:
   the quasi-likelihood $F$ test of
   @lundDetectingDifferentialExpression2012 as implemented in
   `glmGamPoi`. The gate is a
   Benjamini–Hochberg threshold on `adj_pval`.
3. Rank the genes that pass by an effect size, the deviance explained
   $R^{2}_{D,g}=1-\mathcal{D}_g(M_1)/\mathcal{D}_g(M_0)$, with the types
   weighted equally as in @eq-fs-equal-type.

```{r}
#| label: fs-omnibus-call
#| eval: false
# Not run. counts: genes x cells of one slot; cell_type: factor over
# cells; lib: full library sizes (10^log_umi). Thresholds are set
# before the ranks are seen.
source("R/rank_genes_omnibus.R")
keep <- presence_gate(counts, cell_type, min_detection = 0.05)
ranked <- rank_genes_omnibus(counts[keep, ], cell_type, library_size = lib)

# The two glmGamPoi calls it wraps:
fit <- glmGamPoi::glm_gp(
  counts[keep, ],
  design = ~cell_type,
  col_data = data.frame(cell_type = cell_type),
  offset = log(lib),
  size_factors = FALSE
)
qlf <- glmGamPoi::test_de(fit, reduced_design = ~1)
```

The wrapper arguments in the chunk are illustrative; the definitive
signatures are those of `R/rank_genes_omnibus.R`. Why a gate followed
by an effect size, rather than a rank by $p$-value, is in
[3.1, omnibus](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-omnibus).

**Calibration and stability (planned, not run).**

| Question | Resampling | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| Is the nominal $F$ tail accurate? | label permutation, one permutation applied to all genes | labels within the slot |
| How stable is the top 500? | nonparametric bootstrap, stratified by type | cells within type |
| Uncertainty of $R^{2}_{D,g}$ | same bootstrap, percentile interval | cells within type |

: Resampling plan for the omnibus rank. The number of replicates is not fixed yet. {#tbl-fs-boot-perm}

Cell types are the authors' annotations, fixed before any statistic is
computed here. Labels refined on the same counts would make every
permutation $p$-value anti-conservative
[@gonzalezDelgadoPostclusteringInference2025].

## 48 h bulk consistency filter {#sec-fs-bulk-consistency}

`bulk_consistency_filter()` (`R/bulk_consistency.R`) removes genes
whose bulk expression cannot be produced by the single-cell reference.
It needs a single-cell slot and a bulk sample of the same condition.
In Suppinger the only such pair is single-cell 48 h (B-S and SBR
pooled) against the standard-Wnt bulk at 48 h, three biological
replicates (@fig-suppinger-design). The early-Wnt bulk has no matched
reference.

- **Fit.** At 48 h only: for each gene, compare the bulk value of each
  replicate with the range that the 48 h type means allow, and flag
  median-absolute-deviation outliers. The thresholds follow
  RNA-Sieve's range bound and outlier rule as described in the
  vignette.
- **Apply.** The flagged genes are removed from the panel at every
  time, including 72 h and 96 h, where no matched pair exists.
- **Status.** A heuristic, labelled as such in the code. No script
  reads the bulk HTSeq table yet (`01_01` does not); the filter has
  not been run.

The model behind the bound, and the alternatives that keep such genes
and down-weight them, are in
[3.1, cross-platform](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-cross-platform).

```{r}
#| label: fs-bulk-consistency-call
#| eval: false
# Not run. sc48: counts of the 48 h slot with labels; bulk48: the three
# standard-Wnt 48 h replicates from GSE229386, same gene identifiers.
source("R/bulk_consistency.R")
flags <- bulk_consistency_filter(sc48, cell_type48, bulk48)
panel <- setdiff(panel, flags$gene[flags$flagged])
```

## Cell-line sensitivity at 48 h {#sec-fs-cell-line}

48 h is the only slot that contains both cell lines. The script
`output/naive_marker_selection/cell_line_48h/01_03_sensitivity_48h_cell_line.R`
refits the same v2 model inside B-S and inside SBR and compares the
equal-cell top 500 and the per-type top 50. (It lives under `output/`
next to its results; `scripts/01_03_export_equal_type_seurat.R` is a
different script.)

- The two global lists share 308 of 500 genes (Jaccard 0.45).
- Epiblast shares 29, and exiting naïve pluripotency 30, of its top 50.
- Naïve pluripotency is scored in SBR only: B-S has fewer than 20 cells
  of that type.

Outputs: `overlap_48h_cell_line.csv`, `ranks_global_48h_by_line.csv`,
`ranks_per_cell_type_48h_by_line.csv`, `venn_48h_cell_line.pdf`.

## Knowledge-driven markers {#sec-fs-markers}

The marker list is curated and short:
`data/dictionaries/mouse_gastruloid_signaling_markers.csv`, with
columns `cell_type_excel` (lineage on the signalling map),
`cell_type_suppinger` (the matching Suppinger label, or `NA`) and
`gene_marker`. Symbols are mapped offline with `org.Mm.eg.db`
(`R/map_marker_symbols.R`), not `biomaRt`.

Fifteen of the 19 mouse symbols are in the 2,944-gene allow-list.
Under a uniform draw of 19 genes from the 27,027 RNA symbols the
expected overlap is about 2.1; the hypergeometric upper tail is
$P(X\ge 15)=8.8\times10^{-12}$ (`marker_sct_hypergeometric.csv`). The
four absent markers are *Myod1*, *Pax6*, *Sox1* and *Tfap2a*
(`venn_markers_vs_counts.pdf`).

Seurat object to the 500 genes of list 2 at each time and writes
`data/intermediate/equal_type_top500_by_time.rds`, the input of every
script of @sec-cov-scope. The object keeps `log_umi` from the full
library; its `nCount_RNA` is recomputed on the 500 genes and must not
be used as a library size.

## Optional multivariate refinement {#sec-fs-nsga2}

A univariate rank ignores redundancy between genes and the
covariances DeCovarT models. The optional stage searches subsets of
the panel with a multi-objective criterion on all types jointly
([3.1, multivariate](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-multivariate)).
It needs $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j}$, so it runs after
@sec-cov-scope, and it is drawn dashed in @fig-pipeline.

Planned settings:

- **Optimiser.** NSGA-II through `mco::nsga2()` [@R-mco]. Genes are
  encoded as a mask in $[0,1]^{G}$, thresholded to a target panel size.
- **Objectives**, all minimised:
  1. the 2-norm condition number $\kappa_{2}(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\mathcal{G}})$
     of the mean signature restricted to the panel;
  2. the mean pairwise `MixSim` overlap of the $J$ Gaussians
     $\mathcal{N}(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j},\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j})$
     [@melnykovMixSimPackageSimulating2012; @R-MixSim];
  3. optionally, minus the smallest eigenvalue of the Fisher
     information for $\boldsymbol{p}$, as a sensitivity objective on a
     shortlist of non-dominated panels.
- **Output.** The whole Pareto front, not one panel. With one
  specimen, any panel chosen here is fitted on this atlas and has to
  be challenged on an external gastruloid cohort.

`scripts/04_02_feature_selection_genetic_algorithm.R` is a template:
it stops with an error until the fitness function is implemented on a
real panel.

```{r}
#| label: fs-nsga2-sketch
#| eval: false
# Not run. mu: G x J means; Sigma: list of J covariances (G x G), both
# on the linear scale, from the estimator selected in the covariance
# chapter.
fitness <- function(mask) {
  g <- which(mask > 0.5)
  kappa2 <- kappa(mu[g, , drop = FALSE], exact = TRUE)
  ov <- MixSim::overlap(
    Pi = rep(1 / J, J),
    Mu = t(mu[g, , drop = FALSE]),
    S = simplify2array(lapply(Sigma, \(A) A[g, g, drop = FALSE]))
  )
  c(kappa2, mean(ov$OmegaMap[upper.tri(ov$OmegaMap)]))
}
front <- mco::nsga2(fitness, idim = nrow(mu), odim = 2L,
  lower.bounds = rep(0, nrow(mu)), upper.bounds = rep(1, nrow(mu)))
```

## What is not run {#sec-fs-not-run}

::: {#nte-pseudoreplication .callout-warning}
## :warning: Cells of one specimen are not biological replicates

GSE229513 has one specimen series. Cells, or random partitions of
cells, are technical draws; resampling them measures sampling
variability inside the specimen, not variability between organoids
[@squairConfrontingFalseDiscoveries2021;
@zimmermanPracticalSolutionPseudoreplication2021]. No calibrated
differential-expression claim is made in this book. The bulk series
GSE229386 does have three biological replicates per time and schedule;
they support bulk contrasts, not single-cell ones.
:::

The following were considered and are not part of the pipeline. Each
is reviewed in
[3.1, review](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-review).

- Pseudo-bulk `DESeq2`, `edgeR` or `limma`–voom: no biological
  replicates at the level of the contrast (@nte-pseudoreplication).
- `MAST` hurdle tests: droplet UMI counts are modelled without a
  zero-inflation layer (@nte-drop-zico).
- Differential-network screens (`INDEED`, D-trace) and Markov-boundary
  growth of marker seeds: they need fitted graphs and belong to the
  perspectives of the covariance vignette
  ([3.3, perspectives](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-3-precision-networks.html#sec-cov-perspectives)).
